skill.name: marketing-strategy-pmm
skill.description: Create product marketing strategy for B2B SaaS teams, including ICP definition, positioning, messaging, launch planning, competitive battlecards, win/loss analysis, sales enablement, and international market entry.
skill.summary: Guides B2B SaaS PMM work from positioning and ICPs to launches, battlecards, and market entry plans.
skill.author: alirezarezvani

security_audit.summary: All static findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences, inline placeholders, and ordinary GTM planning language. No evidence found for prompt injection, command execution intent, data exfiltration, network scanning, or hidden operational code in SKILL.md.

content.value_statement: Product teams often need clear positioning, launch plans, and sales enablement without rebuilding every framework. This skill turns product, market, and competitor inputs into structured PMM strategy outputs.
actual_capabilities: Defines ICPs, buyer personas, and segmentation for B2B SaaS teams.
Applies April Dunford positioning steps to product and market inputs.
Builds messaging hierarchy, value propositions, and persona-specific messages.
Plans 90-day GTM launches with channels, tasks, budgets, and metrics.
Creates competitive battlecard, win/loss, and sales enablement structures.
Guides international market entry for the US, UK, DACH, France, and Canada.
limitations: It does not connect to HubSpot, Google Analytics, Gong, or competitor websites.
It requires user-supplied product, customer, market, and competitor data.
Example budgets and benchmarks need validation against current business data.
The scanned package contains one Markdown playbook; referenced resources may not be included.

use_cases.title: Position a New B2B SaaS Product
use_cases.description: Turn product strengths, target segments, and alternatives into a clear category, value proposition, and messaging hierarchy.

use_cases.title: Plan a 90-Day GTM Launch
use_cases.description: Create launch phases, channel tasks, success metrics, and post-launch optimization steps for a new product or major feature.

use_cases.title: Enable Sales Against Competitors
use_cases.description: Build battlecards, objection handling, proof points, and win/loss questions for sales teams in competitive deals.

prompt_templates.title: Define an ICP
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a target segment.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to define an ICP for our B2B SaaS product. Ask for missing product, customer, market, and pricing details first.

prompt_templates.title: Create Positioning
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate positioning work for a product or feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the April Dunford method to position our product. Include alternatives, unique attributes, customer value, target customers, category, and trends.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Launch Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Detailed GTM planning for a product launch.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 90-day GTM launch plan for our product. Include pre-launch, launch, post-launch, channels, sales enablement, and success metrics.

prompt_templates.title: Design Market Expansion
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning across regions and competitors.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build an international market entry and competitive enablement plan. Compare US, UK, DACH, France, and Canada, then recommend priorities and sales assets.

output_examples.input: We are launching an AI workflow feature for mid-market SaaS companies.
output: Recommended launch tier: major launch with eight weeks of preparation.
Primary audience: operations leaders and technical buyers in mid-market SaaS.
Core message: reduce manual workflow work while improving team visibility.
Key assets: landing page, demo script, sales deck, battlecard, and customer proof.

output_examples.input: We need positioning against a broad incumbent competitor.
output: Competitive alternative: incumbent suite, spreadsheets, and internal tools.
Differentiation angle: faster time-to-value and focused workflow depth.
Proof needed: onboarding time, adoption rate, support quality, and customer results.
Sales talk track: qualify the buyer pain before comparing feature lists.

output_examples.input: We want to expand from the US into Europe next year.
output: Suggested order: UK first, then DACH, then France based on localization effort.
Preparation: pricing localization, GDPR review, local proof, and partner research.
Success metrics: regional pipeline, win rate, sales cycle, and marketing payback.

best_practices: Provide product, ICP, pricing, competitor, and launch stage details before requesting strategy.
Validate claims, metrics, budgets, and proof points with internal source data.
Review outputs with product, sales, customer success, legal, and finance stakeholders.
anti_patterns: Asking for a generic strategy without product, market, customer, or competitor context.
Treating example benchmarks, budgets, or timelines as guaranteed forecasts.
Publishing competitive claims before collecting evidence and completing legal review.

faq.question: What type of teams should use this skill?
faq.answer: It is best for B2B SaaS teams that need positioning, launches, competitive enablement, or market entry planning.

faq.question: Does it run marketing campaigns automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides strategy, templates, checklists, and planning guidance for humans to execute.

faq.question: Can it create competitive battlecards?
faq.answer: Yes. It can structure competitor overview, strengths, weaknesses, talk tracks, proof points, and sales guidance.

faq.question: Does it need company data?
faq.answer: Yes. Better inputs about customers, pricing, competitors, product strengths, and goals produce better outputs.

faq.question: Can it support international GTM planning?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for US, UK, DACH, France, and Canada market entry decisions.

faq.question: Is it safe for sensitive business plans?
faq.answer: Use the same data handling rules as your AI environment. Remove confidential details when policy requires it.
